effect: The cells made supporting fibres around themselves, completing the last goal. The result contrasted proteins kept inside muscle cells with material released around supporting cells.
reaction: The contrast helped the two paths feel connected rather than just repeated.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the pulling proteins was most worthwhile: the picture showed how overlapping fibres can slide to shorten a cell, connecting the new proteins to a job.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second messenger-and-amino-acid sequence felt somewhat repetitive once the muscle path had shown the pattern, though its different result was useful.

surprise.text: It was interesting that cells with the same chromosomes could use different instructions and end up making proteins for different jobs.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the messenger pictures and the earlier protein-building example gave the pairings a purpose.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how these cells become larger tissues, especially how the muscle cells are assembled. The protein fibres gave me a clear reason to be curious.
